title: Research work and its reports: readers first, then report content
why: M03 adds a second native task kind, research, whose result is a report: one artifact authored in Markdown with versions v1..vN and other formats (a PDF) as renditions of a version (migration 0022). This part is the read side only. Every reader that would refuse a research task, a Markdown report or a rendition learns them before any writer exists (plan §5, readers first).

Old records read exactly as before: a property this amendment adds is omitted when it has no value, never sent as null, so an older Studio or bridge reads every record that existed before M03 unchanged. Records only a later M03 release can write (a research task, a Markdown report, a rendition) need these readers, so that release follows the one carrying them.

A bridge result's kind is any bounded kind name, not a closed list: a bridge acts on the kinds it knows and leaves any other result unannounced, so a later task kind never fails a whole assignment batch.

Report content (part 2): getSourceContent authorizes each read of a report's source or rendition and answers with its hash, size, type and a file name. A text kept inline (at most 256 KiB, source_texts) comes back as text; stored bytes come back as a URL that expires, signed by the API, which alone holds the store's credential (D5). The client checks the bytes it received against the hash before showing or saving them. disposition=attachment makes the URL save the file under its name.

Knowledge (part 2): listReports lists report cards, newest first, from one project or from every project the reader is a member of (L6). It has a format filter and a search over the title, the description and the version notes, never the report bodies. Counts and project names come only from projects the reader can read. listArtifactVersions answers every version of one report with its notes, newest first. The deterministic change facts and the trigger join both reads when publication writes them (S4).

Execution policy (S2): a runtime command's role may name a specialization (sophia-research-md-v1), and a create may name the route admission chose for it. The bridge runs the route its own unit maps to the role and refuses a create whose route differs, so the route is never taken from the wire alone. The runtime wire changes with the research runtime unit (sophia-runtime-m03-dev); an older bridge refuses a role it does not define, as before.

S4: the write side. A runtime advertises its specialist roles in hello; start_research admits research; the runtime research operations (context, reserve, settle, capture, draft) let the research tools read the task, spend from its allowance, keep what they retrieved with its provenance and write a draft, authenticated and fenced like observations.

The guide's tool surface is versioned: GET /v1/media/tool-surface?guide=v1.2 names start_research, and without the parameter it answers v1.1's six operations exactly as before, so a bridge running the M01 guide still activates against this API.

S4 part 3: a research task ends through runtimeResearchSubmit, never through its last message: the result publishes the current draft as the report's next stable version with its checks, notes and change facts, or a blocker records why it stopped and what remains.

S4 part 4: a version carries the facts the service computed at publication (sections added, revised, removed and kept; whether the conclusion changed; sources added and dropped), and its notes must agree with them. A research task's detail carries its progress (allowance and source policy). A version lists the sources it cites with their provenance. Members edit a report's description with attribution.

S5a part 2: a render job is a research task's child, carrying a source package (one HTML entry and its images, each a stored source by relative path and SHA-256). The supervisor on the renderer host holds only a render runner capability: it claims under a lease, fetches each file and uploads the PDF through the API (never a storage URL or key), and settles with the kernel's receipt. A Hold returns a render to the queue, a Stop cancels it, and a render that ends after either is never the job's result.
